history: 5da382fd59222819cff110f85ca738a74fb335d1 feat(skills): require explicit merge modes (#10978)

notes: Lines 1-100 are import surface only. The service directly couples filesystem and hashing, Drizzle/database tables, adapter-utils preference persistence and a very broad shared Skill/API type vocabulary; this is already a high-responsibility orchestration module rather than a narrow domain service.
The earlier attempt to display lines 1-250 was truncated by the tool and is not counted as reviewed evidence; lines are credited only as the smaller ranges become fully visible.

Lines 101-200 add direct dependencies on instance-root resolution, HTTP error construction, GitHub transport, Agents, Projects, Folders, Documents, Work Products, catalog/provenance and portable-path services. Persistence rows are reshaped through large hand-maintained Pick projections, increasing schema/API drift risk and confirming this unit owns many unrelated lifecycles.

Lines 201-300 define import/persist DTOs and an explicit replace/rename/skip conflict policy. External GitHub/skills.sh sources must pin a 40-hex commit and any external source classified scripts_executables is rejected, which is a strong supply-chain default; URL sources are exempt from commit pinning and the check relies on upstream trust-level classification.

Lines 301-400 reserve bundled Paperclip keys, define extensive provenance/update/audit metadata, explicit missing-local-source markers, workspace scan targets, runtime materialization/version options and a coarse Agent/User/System actor. Provenance is stored in an open metadata record rather than a typed immutable lifecycle; the actor shape has identity IDs but no accountable-human or authority/evidence binding.

Lines 401-500 introduce a process-local promise map for inventory refresh deduplication, a full-column Skill selector, a broad allowlist of agent-tool project directories, and project-root inclusion of references/scripts/assets. Catalog file size is capped at 1 MiB, but no aggregate archive/directory limits appear in this segment. Process-local coordination cannot by itself serialize multiple server replicas.

Lines 501-600 normalize package paths and identity keys, compute deterministic inventory hashes, derive collision suffixes and runtime names, and begin a byte-preserving frontmatter-name rewrite. Hash-based runtime suffixes use only 10 hex characters (naming, not integrity), while unique key/slug generation consults caller-maintained sets and therefore still needs database uniqueness/concurrency handling later.

Lines 601-700 derive canonical keys from flexible frontmatter/metadata and source identity, then classify inventory files by directory/extension. Local and URL identities embed a 10-hex locator hash, tying identity to machine paths or URLs and allowing theoretical collisions; script detection is extension/list based and omits executables without recognized suffixes, shebang/content analysis and several executable ecosystems.

Lines 701-800 derive trust entirely from inventory classification, wrap GitHub fetches, resolve default branches/commits and parse/normalize remote URLs. HTTPS and credential/query/fragment rejection are good; remote error messages include full URLs, branch fallback silently assumes main, and parsing accepts arbitrary hostnames as GitHub-shaped pending later checks. Trust remains file-type risk classification, not publisher/content/integrity trust.

Lines 801-900 pin symbolic refs, tokenize a narrow npx skills add syntax without executing it, and canonicalize registry/key imports to GitHub. The parser intentionally ignores most command tokens, which is safer than shelling out, but quote handling is simplistic and warnings remain unused in this segment. Skills.sh is treated as discovery provenance while GitHub becomes the fetched source.

Lines 901-1000 enforce HTTPS for explicit schemes, detect generic Git-like sources, locate bundled roots through several runtime-relative candidates and start deriving source provenance from frontmatter metadata. Generic repository detection accepts any HTTPS host/path as a Git repo; provenance fields are accepted from untrusted skill metadata and require later verification before they can be authoritative.

Lines 1001-1100 finish URL/catalog provenance derivation, parse inline package Skills, assign every co-located file under each Skill directory to its inventory and recursively walk local directories while skipping only .git and node_modules. Inline inventory contains path/kind but no size/digest here; recursive traversal has no visible depth/file-count/byte limit and follows directory entries based on Dirent classification, requiring later symlink and containment checks.

Lines 1101-1200 implement lexical plus realpath containment, reject symlinks along the selected path and recursively in admitted trees, require a regular SKILL.md, and produce sanitized user-facing scan failures. This is careful workspace escape prevention. Remaining concerns include TOCTOU between validation/read, hard links/mount aliases, unbounded traversal, and error strings embedding absolute local paths before the sanitized scan wrapper.

Lines 1201-1300 collect path/kind-only local inventories, compare them without content hashes, provide deterministic JSON comparison, and begin bundled-skill folder/metadata normalization. Inventory equality cannot detect content-only changes, so it is unsuitable as integrity or update evidence unless a later stage refreshes digests.

Lines 1301-1400 compare nearly every persisted field to avoid unnecessary updates and begin local-directory import. When workspaceRoot is absent, the import skips containment/symlink validation entirely; it reads SKILL.md before collecting inventory and overlays caller metadata after parsed metadata, enabling trusted caller context to override sourceKind but not providing a content snapshot or atomic read.

Lines 1401-1500 discover root, explicit and known-tool Skill directories. Explicit paths are realpathed and containment checked; automatic directory roots, however, accept symlinked entries whose targets are directories and add their resolved lexical path before later validation. Selection normalization rejects absolute and dot segments, and the NUL-delimited workspace/path key avoids simple concatenation ambiguity.

Lines 1501-1600 import arbitrary local files/directories and begin remote repository ingestion. Direct local imports again lack workspace containment and symlink validation, recurse without bounds, and derive each nested Skill inventory by prefix, so a parent Skill can absorb nested Skills/files. GitHub ingestion requests the entire recursive tree before filtering, with no truncation flag, entry-count or repository-size handling visible yet.

Lines 1601-1700 fetch only each SKILL.md body while inventories claim every repository blob under its directory. Thus trust classification can see script paths, but file content/digests are not fetched or verified at import. Generic HTTPS markdown imports become markdown-only single-file Skills with no immutable sourceRef, publisher proof or response size/content-type controls visible here.

Lines 1701-1800 map permissive database JSON/enums to API models and normalize sharing/categories. Inventory entry kinds and several enums are type-cast without runtime allowlisting; unknown sharing values default to company, which is a fail-open visibility choice. Public-link writes are disabled even though rows/tokens remain modeled.

Lines 1801-1900 normalize storefront metadata with length caps and serialize full version file contents into database JSON. URL-like icon/homepage fields are length-limited but not scheme/host validated here. Version inventories preserve content but still type-cast kind/path values; this creates a potentially large database payload and needs total-size limits and secret scanning elsewhere.

Lines 1901-2000 define a built-in natural-language test harness that asks an Agent not to cause durable/external effects, plus a constrained placeholder renderer and coarse run-status normalization. Prompt instructions are not a security boundary: no sandbox, capability denial, data egress rule or accountable-human approval is established here, so the claim of a read-only/default-safe harness must depend on later runtime enforcement.

Lines 2001-2100 project test-run state/cost, compare version snapshots by sorted JSON, model missing local sources in mutable metadata and begin reference resolution. Unknown stored run states silently become queued, which can misrepresent corruption/new states; missing-source detectedAt is sensibly preserved across repeat reconciliation but is not an immutable event.

Lines 2101-2200 resolve requested Skills by stable ID, normalized key or unique slug, report ambiguity explicitly, normalize desired version selection and verify a version belongs to both company and Skill. This is a sound tenant/version binding check, though returned selection order is deduplicated by Set and error details expose supplied identifiers.

Lines 2201-2300 optionally preserve stale unknown desired keys while always rejecting ambiguous slugs, then map Agent config preferences to canonical keys/version entries. This honest stale-reference behavior is useful for operator remediation. Resolution performs one database query per selected version, creating an avoidable N+1 path for larger Agent skill sets.

Lines 2301-2400 resolve runtime/local paths, detect missing sources sequentially, scope managed rename targets to a direct company-owned directory and begin byte-level audit collection. Error detail exposes absolute source paths, missing checks are sequential filesystem I/O, and resolveLocalSkillFilePath does not itself prove the normalized child remains within the Skill root—safety depends on normalizePortablePath semantics and callers.

Lines 2401-2500 recursively read every regular file into memory, reject symlinks/path escapes, perform a basic binary heuristic and extract markdown links with regex before starting installed-byte audit. There are still no traversal depth/file-count/per-file/aggregate-byte caps; lstat size is recorded before read, so TOCTOU and memory exhaustion remain possible. Markdown-link regex is intentionally shallow and not a full parser.

Lines 2501-2600 compute full installed content hashes, compare recorded paths, validate basic frontmatter and scan text using regex heuristics for remote execution, secret exfiltration, network and secret references. This is useful defense-in-depth but not a sandbox or robust static analysis: patterns have easy false negatives/positives, oversized files are read before rejection, assets bypass content scanning, and warnings do not establish approval/data-egress policy.

Lines 2601-2700 infer display languages and source editability. Remote/bundled sources are read-only while local/project files are editable. Managed-root detection uses string startsWith rather than path containment, so a sibling such as <managedRoot>-evil can be misclassified editable/Paperclip-owned; source labels expose local paths and editability is a UI/service projection, not authorization.

Lines 2701-2800 enrich list/detail/fork projections and infer divergence from version count or mutable userModifiedAt metadata. Fork authorship is actor-relative but stored in metadata, while summaries expose source locators/tokens upstream. Divergence is a heuristic, not a verified three-way comparison to origin/current upstream.

Lines 2801-2900 finish list projections, batch last-editor lookup with company-scoped Agent join, construct the large service and begin local-source authorization. Last editor can be a User or Agent but has no accountable human/role context; the query is sensibly batched and deterministically ordered.

Lines 2901-3000 complete approved-root authorization using canonical paths, silently swallow bundled import errors, validate release-manifest containment and start materializing complete version files. The approved-root check is strong for the explicit import service path. Bundled failures returning an empty set hide corruption/packaging faults; version collection reads every file as UTF-8 without limits or binary handling.

Lines 3001-3100 verify immutable bundled release snapshots by content hash, create missing versions, reconcile category folders and begin local-source reconciliation. Release integrity checking is strong after seeding but has no signature/publisher proof. Folder and source reconciliation execute many per-item updates/filesystem scans without a transaction or batching.

Lines 3101-3200 mark missing-but-used local Skills for remediation, but automatically delete missing-and-unused library rows plus runtime materializations during ordinary inventory refresh. This destructive lifecycle is triggered by list/read paths, has no grace period, approval, tombstone or audit event, and can race multi-replica refreshes because deduplication is process-local. Every list also runs company existence, bundled release/folder and filesystem reconciliation before querying.

Lines 3201-3300 implement all search/filter/category/attachment counting/sorting in memory after loading every Skill, folder and Agent. Attached counts recompute desired Skill resolution for every Skill×Agent pair, making the list O(S×A×S-reference-resolution) and unpaginated. Search intentionally overrides folder filtering, a subtle UI semantic encoded in service logic.

Lines 3301-3400 provide company-scoped ID/key/unique-slug/version reads, folder enrichment, actor-relative stars and generic metadata patching. Most tenant predicates are sound, but updateSkillMetadata updates only by Skill ID and trusts the already-loaded object; it has no optimistic revision and can lose concurrent metadata fields despite merge-on-stale-object behavior.

Lines 3401-3500 persist audit/update-hold metadata, compute desired-only Agent usage, count versions and assemble detail/fork prechecks. Audit is limited to local/catalog sources and mutates metadata after scan without CAS. Existing fork summaries issue one count query per fork (N+1); usage deliberately avoids runtime truth, so desired and actual deployment remain distinct.

Lines 3501-3600 snapshot version contents via one read per inventory entry and create monotonically numbered versions inside a row-lock transaction. Row locking plus company predicates is a solid concurrency pattern for revision allocation/current pointer updates. Snapshot collection happens before the transaction and is not atomic with mutable files; actor IDs are recorded but authority/responsibility/evidence are not.

Lines 3601-3700 implement star counters and threaded comments. Stars use check-then-insert and separately recompute denormalized counts, so correctness relies on a database uniqueness constraint and concurrent refreshes can write stale counts. Any board User is considered able to mutate any comment at this service layer, while Agents may edit only their own; role/permission enforcement must exist outside.

Lines 3701-3800 soft-delete comments and plan fork reassignments. Comment mutation is company/Skill scoped but has no optimistic version/history preservation for edits. Reassignment loads terminated Agents too, verifies company and current desired use, and reports precise failures; it does not yet establish accountable approval for changing Agent capabilities.

Lines 3801-3900 apply Agent reassignments under row locks in one database transaction and define compensating cleanup for failed forks. Transactional config changes are strong, but selected pinned versions are reset to null on fork. Cleanup commits database deletion before filesystem deletion; a filesystem failure leaves orphaned bytes, and neither reassignment nor cleanup emits an immutable activity/evidence record here.

Lines 3901-4000 implement a non-transactional filesystem→database→version→Agent fork saga. It force-deletes the chosen fork directory before creation, copies text-only file detail, mutates counts separately and only compensates reassignment failures—not earlier partial failures. Slug/key uniqueness is based on a stale in-memory snapshot, so concurrent forks can target the same directory; robust DB uniqueness alone cannot protect bytes already overwritten.

Lines 4001-4100 begin managed rename with no-op detection, in-memory conflict checks, directory existence guard, preserved version pins and a reversible filesystem-first stage followed by a DB transaction. The design explicitly plans compensation and is stronger than fork, but conflict checks remain race-prone and absolute directory paths leak in errors.

Lines 4101-4200 complete rename compensation, purge stale runtime materialization and begin update-status computation. Rollback failures are swallowed, so a failed DB transaction can still leave filesystem identity inconsistent; post-commit runtime deletion failure surfaces after durable rename. Update status reruns the full byte audit and uses catalog content hashes, correctly separating supported/unsupported tracking states.

Lines 4201-4300 resolve GitHub update refs and implement inventory-gated file reads across local/catalog/GitHub/URL sources. Remote files are fetched lazily from the pinned ref, which is good, but local path containment still depends on normalized inventory entries and files are decoded as UTF-8 regardless of asset/binary kind. Missing remote SKILL.md falls back to the stored body, making availability resilient but potentially hiding source drift/outage.

Lines 4301-4400 update storefront fields without optimistic concurrency and begin managed Skill creation/fork copying. Creation checks database key then force-deletes the target directory, repeating the fork race/data-loss hazard: concurrent or orphaned directory state can be destroyed before authoritative uniqueness is established. URL fields still lack scheme validation, and copied assets are treated as UTF-8 text.

Lines 4401-4500 finish creation through several non-atomic filesystem/DB/count/version steps and begin direct file editing. A failure can leave a directory, Skill row, counters or missing initial version out of sync; there is no compensation. Editable is derived metadata, then arbitrary normalized paths are written with no content/size/type/risk approval or expected-content revision at this point.

Lines 4501-4600 update metadata after a file write, create a version only when content changed, and implement file/folder deletion followed by version creation. Both are filesystem-first non-atomic sagas: DB/version failure leaves unversioned changes, and concurrent edits have no expected hash/revision. Internal updates filter only by Skill ID. Deletion protects SKILL.md but does not capture deleted bytes as explicit evidence beyond the post-delete snapshot.

Lines 4601-4700 gate updates on audit findings/local modifications, allow force-discard, audit a catalog origin snapshot, copy it into the live managed directory and then update DB metadata. Preflight audit is valuable, but copy→DB→post-audit is non-atomic; a failed post-audit leaves the new bytes and DB state installed, merely marks failure, and force has no responsibility/approval record here.

Lines 4701-4800 re-import remote updates and implement catalog reset from a pinned, hash-verified origin snapshot. Origin verification and explicit force requirement are strong recovery safeguards. Reset still copies over the live directory before DB update and records no pre-reset immutable version/evidence in this segment, so database failure can leave untracked destructive restoration.

Lines 4801-4900 post-audit reset, browse a company-scoped local project workspace and begin scan orchestration. Browse uses realpath containment, excludes symlinks/.git/node_modules and caps output at 250. It slices filesystem enumeration before sorting, so which entries are omitted is platform/order dependent; per-directory isSkill checks also cause up to 250 sequential stats.

Lines 4901-5000 normalize selective scan requests, gather company project/workspace targets and start sequential discovery. Invalid selections are retained for later reporting, and company scoping comes through Projects. Warnings expose configured absolute workspace paths, all projects/workspaces are traversed serially, and remote_managed exclusion used by browse is not visible in scan target construction.

Lines 5001-5100 validate each discovered directory with workspaceRoot, sanitize import errors, recognize same-path/bundled duplicates and allow explicit renaming. Same-source refresh preserves the existing key/slug, which is stable. Candidate/skipped outputs still expose directory paths; selected renamed keys use only a short path hash and are machine-location-derived.

Lines 5101-5200 detect key/slug conflicts against the evolving accepted set and update same-source entries. Conflict reporting is explicit and prevents silent overwrite, but returns both existing/new absolute source locators. The WebSocket path is useful real-time infrastructure, but company-wide delivery requires strong server membership authorization and should use stable envelopes, resumable cursors and explicit sequence-gap recovery before Company OS treats it as an operational or evidentiary feed.

notes: Lines 1-200 establish a broad worktree test surface spanning Git subprocesses, networking/port reservation, direct database tables, embedded PostgreSQL, configuration/database/storage/Secret copying, routine pausing, execution-state quarantine, workspace cwd rebinding and reseed/init/make/repair commands. This is a deployment and data-lifecycle subsystem, not a simple Git helper.

The tests deliberately prefer a repository-local .paperclip/config.json over an ambient PAPERCLIP_CONFIG and begin verifying discovery from nested working directories. This reduces accidental cross-worktree targeting, but the boundary still processes host paths/config/Secret keys and must defend against symlinks, untrusted repositories and incorrect root discovery.

Lines 201-400 validate instance/name sanitization, home-rooted targets, pnpm executable reuse, Git branch/start-point argument construction, URL port rewriting, isolated database/storage/env paths, attachment fallback across storage roots and minimal-versus-full database seeding. Disabling backups and dropping Run/event/session/runtime history for minimal seeds are sensible isolation/performance choices, but importing config-derived executable paths, Git refs and storage objects still needs trust/canonicalization. Returning null for an attachment missing from every store risks silent evidence loss unless the eventual plan reports it as an explicit integrity failure or approved omission.

Lines 401-600 implement a marker-and-lock seeding protocol: success atomically moves pending to complete, failure retains pending and removes the lock, concurrent callers serialize, and a stale lock owned by an exited PID fails closed rather than auto-reclaiming. This is a strong recoverability/idempotency pattern. However PID identity alone is vulnerable to PID reuse, lock-file tampering and cross-host/shared-filesystem ambiguity; Company OS should add an unguessable fencing token, process-start/host/node identity, safe ownership/permissions and an explicit operator recovery command with receipt. The segment begins an embedded-PostgreSQL execution-quarantine test.

Lines 601-800 specify execution quarantine: copied running Agents become idle with timer heartbeat disabled; in-progress Work becomes blocked, Agent assignments/locks are cleared, queued/review Agent assignments are removed, human assignment is retained, and a quarantine comment is appended. The safety intent is strong, but clearing Agent linkage must preserve the prior executor and source Run as immutable provenance rather than only free-text comment evidence. More critically, the seed copies the source local_encrypted master key—or an inline master key—into the new worktree and begins persisting the current Agent JWT secret. This clones the source trust domain into a development branch; Company OS must instead rebind/re-encrypt Secrets under a new deployment/node key, issue separate short-lived runtime identity, and never copy privileged signing keys by default.

Lines 801-1000 confirm the Agent JWT signing Secret is written verbatim into the worktree .env and verify authenticated user rows are cloned into a minimally seeded instance, while force initialization preserves repo-managed checkout directories and sibling-config ports are reserved. Preserving user records may support local testing, but together with copied encryption/JWT keys it creates an identity clone capable of accepting source credentials and decrypting source Secrets. Company OS development/FDE branches must default to synthetic or explicitly re-enrolled principals, new issuer/audience/signing keys, revoked source sessions and sanitized personal data; checkout preservation and port reservation are good non-destructive isolation tests.

Lines 1001-1200 finish sibling port isolation, prefer repo-local source configuration, preserve explicit source paths across cwd changes, require exactly one explicit reseed source and reject targets lacking worktree env identity. These are good fail-closed target-selection guards. Full seeds choose an automatic/streaming backup path while minimal transformed seeds choose JavaScript, exposing two restore engines whose semantic equivalence, size limits and rollback require later evidence. The reseed integration setup begins and explicitly writes a source Secret key, so identity/Secret cloning remains the highest-risk boundary.

Lines 1201-1400 verify reseed preserves target ports/instance branding and restores config/env/instance data after an invalid source failure—a strong rollback contract, though crash/power-loss and rollback failure remain unproved. Workspace cwd rebinding is constrained to descendants of the source repository, while external paths become null, which is safer than copying host paths. Shared Git hooks and auxiliary forbidden-token files are copied executable into the new worktree; this preserves policy but also transfers arbitrary executable code from the source repository trust domain, requiring ownership/integrity review, explicit allowlisting and no automatic execution for untrusted checkouts.

Lines 1401-1600 test end-to-end Git worktree creation, primary-checkout repair no-op, repair of missing metadata and creation of a missing branch worktree. Non-destructive primary behavior is good, but repairing a linked worktree explicitly removes stale instance data before recreating metadata when noSeed is set; this needs preview, exact target proof, recoverable backup and operator receipt in Company OS tooling. The segment begins a database integration test that pauses only Routines with enabled schedule triggers, reflecting a useful activation-safety distinction between scheduled and API-only automation.

Lines 1601-1675 complete the scheduled-Routine quarantine test: only active Routines with enabled schedule triggers pause, while API-only, already paused, archived and disabled-schedule records retain state. This is a precise activation-safety policy worth adapting for cloned/offline environments, but it still directly mutates database state and must preserve actor/reason/source deployment, trigger revision and an auditable reactivation workflow.

Focused execution in the default sandbox produced 31 passed, 8 failed and 4 skipped: six failures were caused by denied local socket probes exhausting the port search to 65536, while two were macOS /var versus /private/var path identity assertions. An elevated rerun removed all six port-related failures and produced 37 passed, 2 failed and 4 skipped; the two remaining failures are the realpath/logical-path mismatch. Embedded PostgreSQL could not start after five attempts even outside the sandbox, so its four tests remain explicitly unverified. CLI no-emit TypeScript passed.

The confirmed credential-exfiltration chain is complete: ancestor-discovered context controls apiBase and apiKeyEnvVarName; common.ts reads process.env[profile.apiKeyEnvVarName]; PaperclipApiClient attaches the value as a Bearer token to apiBase. Explicit --api-key is also exposed in argv and therefore process listings/shell history, while buildCliCommandLabel can persist it in an auth challenge.

common.ts lines 101-200 only trim trailing slashes from API origins, so scheme/TLS/userinfo/host are unrestricted. apiPath correctly rejects empty dynamic segments and percent-encodes them. MIME inference is extension-only and explicitly coupled to a server allowlist, making upload admission drift-prone and incapable of content sniffing or polyglot protection.

Credential precedence is explicit flag -> PAPERCLIP_API_KEY -> profile-named arbitrary environment variable -> plaintext stored board credential. There is no issuer/audience/company/expiry check before transmission. Interactive recovery gates on 401 or two English 403 messages, while the lower HTTP client will replay the original request after recovery; non-idempotent mutation safety remains absent.

common.ts lines 201-298 print arbitrary server objects and scalar fields directly. JSON output and inline rendering have no sensitivity classification; error handling prints server error.message and JSON-stringified details before process.exit, which can leak Secrets/PII and makes English text a client contract. inferApiBaseFromConfig trusts PAPERCLIP_SERVER_HOST and constructs plaintext HTTP without URL validation; malformed hosts, delimiters or credentials can alter the destination. Company OS needs an explicit verified endpoint/profile rather than inference for privileged operations.

Authentication uses terminalSessionId in the URL and sends the bearer token in the first WebSocket frame, avoiding URL token leakage. Invalid/expired credentials are rejected before provider refresh, and unsupported refreshed payloads consume the terminal credential before any SSH connection.
